newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU gave $2.8 bln to its poorest states in 1996.
newsitem.headline: EU gave $2.8 bln to its poorest states in 1996.

text.p: The European Union allocated almost 2.5 billion ecus ($2.8 billion) last year to schemes to improve the environment and transport networks in the bloc's four poorest states, according to a report issued on Thursday.
In its 1996 Cohesion Fund annual report, the European Commission says the EU subsidies given to Spain, Portugal, Greece and Ireland last year led to the creation of 74,100 new jobs.

The 15.15-billion-ecu ($16.97 billion), six-year Fund was set up in 1993 to help the so-called cohesion countries catch up with their richer neighbours in time for the third stage of economic and monetary union (EMU) -- the introduction of a single currency -- in 1999.
The 1996 report indicates that for the first time, EU funds were split almost equally between environmental and transport projects.

This is likely to please the European Parliament which has consistently complained that too much money is being spent on road schemes, and not enough on urban waste, sewage treatment, nature conservation and schemes to cut industrial pollution.
The EU assembly has yet to give its opinion on the way Cohesion Fund money was spent in 1996.

In a report last week on the use of the 1995 Cohesion Fund, the assembly slammed Spain, which receives over half of the cake every year, for stretching the definition of environment schemes to cover new park benches in the middle of Barcelona.
